description: SENKU is an independent technology-driven team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Inspired by the idea of using knowledge from the past to build a better future, we explore scientific discoveries through software engineering, data analysis, visualization, and artificial intelligence. Our mission is to uncover hidden patterns in Earth's systems using NASA data and transform those discoveries into meaningful insights.
summary:
**Stone to Stars** is an interactive climate observatory that transforms NASA Earth observation data into accessible, scientifically grounded insights.

Using historical climate data from NASA POWER, the application enables users to explore temperature and precipitation patterns for selected locations and time periods through interactive maps, annual charts, and trend visualizations.

Beyond displaying observations, Stone to Stars applies Sen's slope and Mann–Kendall trend analysis with Hamed–Rao autocorrelation correction to help users distinguish long-term climate trends from natural variability. The application also communicates data limitations, missing observations, and statistical uncertainty.

Built with Flutter and FastAPI, Stone to Stars aims to make climate information more understandable and accessible, supporting climate awareness, scientific curiosity, and informed decision-making.
details:
What Stone to Stars does

Stone to Stars is a web and mobile climate observatory designed to make historical Earth observation data easier to explore and interpret.

Users can select a geographic location and time period, retrieve climate observations from NASA POWER, and explore temperature and precipitation through interactive charts and statistical summaries.

How it works

The Flutter application provides a responsive interface with an interactive map, an observatory overview, temperature and precipitation analysis screens, and a methodology section.

A Python FastAPI backend retrieves climate data from NASA POWER and performs statistical analysis. The system uses Sen's slope to estimate the magnitude of trends, the Mann–Kendall approach to evaluate trend significance, and Hamed–Rao correction to account for serial correlation.

The application distinguishes statistically significant findings from inconclusive results and communicates missing data, analysis assumptions, and limitations.

Technologies used

  • Frontend: Flutter and Dart
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI
  • Scientific computing: NumPy, SciPy, and pymannkendall
  • NASA data: NASA POWER
  • Maps: MapTiler and Flutter Map
  • Deployment: Netlify for the web frontend and Vercel for the backend
  • Platforms: Web and Android

Creativity and impact

Stone to Stars combines NASA Earth observation data, interactive geographic exploration, and transparent statistical analysis in one accessible experience.

Rather than presenting climate changes without context, the application emphasizes scientific interpretation, uncertainty, and methodological transparency.

Our goal is to help students, researchers, educators, and communities better understand historical climate patterns and make informed decisions.

Limitations

Historical trends do not establish the causes of observed changes or predict future climate conditions. Results depend on data coverage, selected time periods, statistical assumptions, and the spatial characteristics of the underlying NASA POWER data.

Project Links

Live Web Application: https://senku-stone-to-star.netlify.app

GitHub Source Code: https://github.com/rdarshan927/stone-to-stars

Backend API Documentation: https://nasaspaceappchallengefastapi.vercel.app/docs

Platforms: Web and Android

The GitHub repository contains the Flutter frontend, Python FastAPI backend, climate analysis implementation, and project documentation.
